title: Attention: How Tokens Read Their Context
summary: Attention lets every token look back at the others and pull in what it needs. It is a soft lookup: queries are compared with keys, the scores become weights by softmax, and the output is a weighted average of values. This lesson works it through by hand, then adds the causal mask, multiple heads and the cost.
objectives: Explain queries, keys and values as three learned projections of the same token vectors
Compute scaled dot-product attention softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V by hand for a three-token example
Explain why scores are divided by √d_k using the variance of a dot product
Apply a causal mask and explain why a language model needs it
Describe multi-head attention, count its parameters and estimate the n² cost of attention
prerequisites: You should be comfortable with dot products and cosine similarity ([Embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings)) and with matrix multiplication as a stack of dot products. Softmax is introduced here; it reappears in [Sampling](/learn/model-foundations/sampling).
